result.title: PROPS: Can Visual Generators Keep the Current Look of a Prop?
result.summary: Many generation tasks draw the next image from a visual history, such as storyboards, illustrated stories and multi-turn editing. A new request often states what happens next without restating how earlier objects look. Instead of recovering an object's current look from the history, generators often redraw it from the request alone or bring back an outdated look, and the error can carry into later steps. We call this failure prop drift. Existing evaluations rarely isolate it, because similarity to the history rewards copying and a judge that sees a single history cannot tell a look recovered from that history from one the generator happens to prefer. We introduce PROPS, a benchmark of 2,257 pairs of twin histories that end on the same request but show one prop in two different looks. A pair passes only if the generator draws the matching look on each side and carries out the request, so a look preferred by the generator or the judge passes at most one side. All 34 open and closed systems we test show prop drift, and even systems that carry out the requested action on most sides often lose the current look of the prop. Swapping the planners and editors of agents further shows that both history understanding and image generation limit agent performance. We also build PROPS-Train, 80,250 training chains in four tracks whose targets recover an earlier state or carry scripted changes forward, and fine-tuning on it clearly improves all four tested models. Both datasets will be publicly released.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出「prop drift」这一视觉生成失败模式：多步生成中模型不从历史恢复物体当前外观，而是依请求重绘或用过时外观；作者构建含 2,257 对双生历史的 PROPS 基准加以隔离测量，并发布 PROPS-Train 训练链用于微调，评测 34 个系统均出现该问题。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「双生历史同请求、仅外观不同」的对照设计可供核查能否迁移为判断生成是否真正使用视觉证据与历史状态的因果式评价，而 prop drift 与 LVR 中视觉信息未进入内部状态、状态更新失败的问题形成概念对应；但任务属图像生成，与 latent reasoning 机制仍有距离。
